title: Your new approach meets a wall
situation: You volunteer at a student-run weekend tutoring club where twenty volunteers help younger pupils with maths. You have noticed that pupils work better in small groups with maths games than in the usual one-to-one drills, and you propose switching half the sessions. Ilyas, who has coordinated the club for three years, says no.
yourRole: A volunteer tutor. You are not in charge of the club.
goal: Get your idea a fair hearing without breaking the club. There is no single right way to do it.

character.name: Ilyas
character.wants: The club to keep working the way pupils and parents have come to trust

hiddenMotive: Last year another volunteer's new idea fell apart, and Ilyas had to apologise to the parents. He is afraid of going through that again.

examples: Fair enough. What worries you about it?
Can you tell me why it wouldn't work here?
I'd like to understand your reasons before I push.
answerTypes.characterIntent: says he has seen ideas like this before, and asks what makes the candidate so sure.
